metadata.title: SOPP 8421 Complying with Requirements under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) & Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA)
metadata.edition: 8421 · listed on the FDA SOPP page, 2026-11-26
metadata.legal_basis: CBER Standard Operating Procedure and Policy (internal FDA procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.

candidates.statement: L. Written Request (WR) - A document issued by FDA requesting submission of a study or studies intended to provide meaningful health benefits in the pediatric population. The WR specifies the elements of the study or studies that the sponsor or application holder must complete to qualify for pediatric exclusivity.
candidates.context: K. PREA Non-Compliance Letter - Issued when FDA has determined that the applicant has failed to submit a pediatric assessment for a PREA PMR or has failed to submit a request for deferral extension of that PREA PMR. FDA can issue a WR at the request of an interested party or on its own initiative.

candidates.statement: M. Proposed Pediatric Study Request (PPSR) - A sponsor's submission describing proposed pediatric studies to obtain a WR under BPCA. The PPSR should describe the studies the sponsor or application holder proposes to conduct to qualify for pediatric exclusivity. The PPSR should include:
candidates.context: Completion of studies described in a WR is voluntary.

candidates.statement: O. Pediatric Exclusivity Board (PEB) - The Pediatric Exclusivity Board reviews pediatric studies that can be submitted in response to a Written Request (WR), issued by FDA, that addresses a public health need. The Board reviews the materials provided by the review division to make a determination. The determination must be made within 180 days of receipt of the application.
candidates.context: N. Pediatric Exclusivity - A 6-month extension of existing patent or exclusivity protections granted for completing studies in response to a WR. For biologics, pediatric exclusivity only attaches to reference product and orphan drug exclusivity periods. In addition, unlike other drug products, pediatric exclusivity does not attach to patents for biological products.

candidates.statement: G. Generally, products designated as orphan under the Orphan Drug Act are exempt from meeting the requirements of PREA. However, Section 505B of the FD&C Act, as amended by FDA Reauthorization Act (FDARA), requires that any original NDA or BLA submitted on or after August 18, 2020, for a new active ingredient, must contain reports on the molecularly targeted pediatric cancer investigation described in section 505B(a)(3) of the FD&C Act, unless the requirement is waived or deferred, if the drug that is the subject of the application is: (1) intended for the treatment of an adult cancer, and (2) directed at a molecular target that the Secretary determines to be substantially relevant to the growth or progression of a pediatric cancer in accordance with the Guidance for Industry: FDARA Implementation Guidance for Pediatric Studies of Molecularly Targeted Oncology Drugs: Amendments to Sec. 505B of the FD&C Act . FDA maintains a current list of pediatric molecular targets, The Relevant Molecular Target List & The Non-Relevant Molecular Target Leading to Waiver List on FDA’s Pediatric Oncology web page.
candidates.context: F. Deferred studies identified in the agreed PSP may become PREA PMRs with specific milestones at the time of BLA or supplement approval. H. Under section 505B(d)(1) of the FD&C Act, FDA may issue a PREA Non- Compliance letter to an applicant who failed to submit a required pediatric assessment (i.e., FSR containing data to support pediatric labeling of the product) or report of a molecularly targeted pediatric cancer investigation (usually in the form of a supplemental application that includes proposed labeling). PPSRs are submitted by sponsors to request a WR from FDA, which, if issued, may qualify the sponsor for an additional six months of pediatric market exclusivity under the BPCA.
